newsitem.title: INDIA: India stocks rally seen pausing, focus on Reliance.
newsitem.headline: India stocks rally seen pausing, focus on Reliance.

text.p: India's bubbling stock markets are likely to pause for a breather this week after a sharp surge led by foreign funds since late May, brokers said.
"We're seeing exhaustion setting in," said Ulhas Paymaster, a member-broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), adding that huge volumes were not pushing the market anymore.
"It is a sign of people running without making any progress," he told Reuters.
The benchmark 30-share BSE index ended 53.05 points, or 1.32 percent, up at 4,083.04 last week -- after scaling a new 52-week high of 4,148.86.
A flurry of buying by foreign insitutional investors (FIIs) has powered the index since May 27 when it closed at 3,692.55, analysts said.
They said allocations to India had risen after setbacks in other emerging markets like Thailand, Malaysia and Manila.

"The FIIs have been the only serious investors," said Bharat Dhanki, a partner at brokerage Vrajlal Dhanki. "Indian stocks offer them the best valuations but their investments are being concentrated in index-linked big and mid-cap stocks."
Domestic funds have largely been shuffling portfolios or selling to meet redemptions, he said.
The focus this week will stay on leading firm Reliance Industries Ltd, brokers said.
The petrochemicals giant is scheduled to consider a bonus equity issue -- after a 14-year gap -- on June 26, and market players believe its ratio would influence market sentiment.
"The Reliance bonus will have a profound impact on speculative trades," said Dhanki.
"If it's below expectations the market would fall to 3,900 levels," Paymaster said. "It'll be the trigger for a correction."

Company analysts predict a bonus ratio of three shares for every five held -- the same as it gave previously in 1983. But traders believe Reliance chairman Dhirubhai Ambani may decide on a four-for-five.
"It took 14 years for this bonus to come," said Dhanki. "People know they cannot expect another bonus for at least 10 years. That's why expectations are rising."
Ambani is expected to unveil the bonus announcement at the company's annual general meeting of shareholders on June 26.

The markets would also watch political developments in Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party as its president Laloo Prasad Yadav and a junior minister face corruption charges in a $280 million fodder scandal, traders said.
"There's no nervousness," said trader Rasesh Maniar at brokerage Mukesh Babu Securities. "But political instability fears remain."
